<module id="traffic_light">
    <description>A traffic light system with red, yellow, green indicators and a pedestrian button.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="pass_request">Request signal for pedestrians to cross.</input>
        <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">Internal counter value.</output>
        <output id="red">Red signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
        <output id="yellow">Yellow signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
        <output id="green">Green signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter_value id="idle">State representing the initial condition.</parameter_value>
        <parameter_value id="s1_red">State representing the red light phase.</parameter_value>
        <parameter_value id="s2_yellow">State representing the yellow light phase.</parameter_value>
        <parameter_value id="s3_green">State representing the green light phase.</parameter_value>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="cnt" width_description="[7:0]">Internal counter for timing control.</register>
        <register id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Current state of the traffic light controller.</register>
        <register id="p_red">Previous red signal.</register>
        <register id="p_yellow">Previous yellow signal.</register>
        <register id="p_green">Previous green signal.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= idle;
            end else begin
                case (state)
                    idle: begin
                        state <= s1_red;
                    end
                    s1_red: begin
                        if (cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                        end
                    end
                    s2_yellow: begin
                        if (cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                        end
                    end
                    s3_green: begin
                        if (cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        // Counting logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 10;
            end else if (pass_request && green) begin
                cnt <= 10;
            end else if (!green && p_green) begin
                cnt <= 60;
            end else if (!yellow && p_yellow) begin
                cnt <= 5;
            end else if (!red && p_red) begin
                cnt <= 10;
            end else begin
                cnt <= cnt - 1;
            end
        end
        
        // Assign statements for outputs
        assign clock = cnt;
        
        // Output logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                {red, yellow, green} <= 3'b000;
            end else begin
                {red, yellow, green} <= {p_red, p_yellow, p_green};
            end
        end
    </implementation>
    
    <task>
        <step>Understand the problem requirements and constraints.</step>
        <step>Create a sequential logic block for state transitions based on the given state machine diagram.</step>
        <step>Design a combinational logic block for counting down the internal counter.</step>
        <step>Assign the internal counter to the output clock.</step>
        <step>Implement the logic for updating previous signals and outputs.</step>
        <step>Test the design with different scenarios to ensure proper functionality.</step>
    </task>
</module>
